name: Italian Game
description: A classical opening leading to rich, tactical positions. White develops the bishop to c4 to target the f7 square and exert central pressure.
plans: Control the centre with c3 and d4
Develop all pieces and castle kingside quickly
Look for Ng5 attacking f7, or build a slow positional advantage

branches.name: Giuoco Piano
branches.description: The 'Quiet Game'. Both sides mirror each other with harmonious development. White will play c3-d4 to fight for the centre.
plans: Play c3 then d4 to challenge the centre
Castle kingside before launching any attack
After d4, recapture with exd4 cxd4 and aim for the Italian bishop on c4 or d3

branches.name: Giuoco Piano Main Line
branches.description: Black develops the f6 knight, increasing pressure on e4. White must be careful about the e4 pawn.
plans: Play d4 immediately — the main tabiya of the Giuoco Piano
If exd4 cxd4, bishop retreats to Bb5 or Bd3
Attack the kingside with Ng5 ideas after d4

branches.name: Evans Gambit
branches.description: A swashbuckling gambit! White sacrifices the b-pawn for rapid piece development and a strong centre. Beloved by Morphy and Fischer.
plans: After 4...Bxb4 play c3 to gain time on the bishop
Follow with d4, aiming for a powerful pawn centre
Rapid development and an early attack on the kingside

branches.name: Two Knights Defense
branches.description: Black fights for central control immediately with 3...Nf6, attacking the e4 pawn. White must choose between the aggressive Ng5 or the solid d3/d4.
plans: Play Ng5 attacking f7 — the Fried Liver Attack after 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5 6.Nxf7
Or play the quiet d3 for a solid Italian setup
4.d4 is another option: exd4 5.e5 d5 6.Bb5

branches.name: Hungarian Defense
branches.description: A solid but passive defence. Black avoids the complications of 3...Bc5 and aims for a solid setup. White gets easy equality and more space.
plans: White plays d4 and d5 to gain space
Develop all pieces quickly — Black's position is solid but passive
Use the space advantage to restrict Black's counterplay

name: Caro-Kann Defense
description: A solid and reliable defence against 1.e4. Black establishes a solid pawn centre without the weaknesses of the French Defense. Favoured by Petrosian, Karpov, and Anand.
plans: Black aims for ...d5 to contest the centre
Develop the c8 bishop actively — this is easier than in the French
Long-term: solid pawn structure, endgame advantage

branches.name: Classical Variation
branches.description: Black develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain — the key advantage of the Caro-Kann over the French.
plans: After Ng3 Bg6, play ...Nd7 then ...Ngf6
Castle queenside and counterattack on the queenside
Trade off the 'good' bishop only when it improves your position

branches.name: Advance Variation
branches.description: White gains space with e5. Black must fight for counterplay with ...c5 and ...e6, similar themes to the French but with the bishop outside.
plans: Play ...c5 to strike at the base of White's pawn chain
Manoeuvre the knight to f5 via d7-f6-e4 or d7-b6
Black's active bishop on f5 is a key piece — don't trade it easily
